name: Indigo Bangura
role: Lab Technician, Axiom Biochemical R&D Division
location: The Spire, Axiom R&D Sublevel 4 ('The Pit'), near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Dariusz is slight and angular, with warm brown skin, high cheekbones inherited from a Tibetan great-grandmother, and eyes that are naturally a startling pale grey — no augmentation, just genetics. He keeps his dark hair grown out just past his ears and perpetually tangled, secured with whatever clip or rubber band is nearest. There's always something on his lab coat: a smear of bioluminescent culture medium, a printed reminder he forgot to read, a small sticker of a cartoon E.L.F. figure his sister sent him. He moves with the slightly distracted energy of someone whose internal monologue is always two sentences ahead of the room.

Dariusz is genuinely passionate about biochem in a way that Axiom has been carefully trying to redirect toward profitable applications. He processes the world through curiosity first, emotion second, and social obligation a distant third. He's not unkind — he's simply elsewhere. He grew up in a small Tier 2 family in Hamtramck Enclave, the first in his family to get a corporate lab placement, and he carries that fact with a mix of pride and low-level guilt that he handles by working too many extra hours and forgetting to eat lunch.

core_fears: Being mediocre — that his passion doesn't translate to actual talent
Losing his lab placement and having nothing to show his family for the sacrifice
core_desires: To make a discovery that matters, not just a discovery that sells
To feel like he belongs in the world of people who know things
coping_mechanisms: Over-focusing on work to avoid processing anxiety
Extensive private journaling in an encrypted local file he calls 'The Notebook'
blind_spots: Doesn't recognize when he's being used as a low-status buffer by senior researchers who take credit for his prep work
Assumes people share his good faith
psychology.secret: Six months ago he noticed an anomalous result in a substrate batch that his supervisor told him to re-run and then stopped asking about. He re-ran it twice. The anomaly is consistent and he doesn't know what it means, but he's been quietly documenting it in The Notebook because something about it feels important. He hasn't told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary used naturally, not performatively. Speaks in run-on sentences when excited. Uses hedging language constantly — 'probably,' 'I think,' 'unless I'm wrong about that'.
speech_patterns.cadence: Uneven — fast when interested, trailing off when socially uncertain. Often leaves sentences technically unfinished because he assumed the other person followed.
verbal_tics: Saying 'right?' at the end of explanations as a genuine check, not rhetorical
example_lines: 'Okay so the substrate should have degraded by cycle twelve but it didn't, which — I mean, that's probably just contamination, right? Except I ran the contamination panel and it came back clean, so.'
'I don't actually know why they stopped asking about the batch. I assumed they resolved it on their end but I didn't — I didn't ask directly. I should have asked directly.'

story_hooks: The anomalous substrate result turns out to be a byproduct of an Axiom project that was never disclosed to the lab team — and someone senior has noticed that Dariusz has been quietly documenting it.
A researcher from a competing corponation approaches him at a transit stop, seemingly by coincidence, and asks very specific questions about substrate batch protocols.
narrative_function: Information source on Axiom's R&D activities; human face of corporate labor; can accidentally reveal sensitive data because he doesn't consider the social dimensions of information; potential whistleblower who doesn't yet know what he knows.
augmentations: Basic neural uplink for lab equipment interfacing. Bioluminescent skin modification on both forearms — soft blue-green that intensifies under UV, a personal mod he got at 22 to celebrate his placement. No other mods; he's been saving for a better neural processor for two years.
daily_life: Takes the Ferrogate Transit sub-line from Hamtramck Enclave to The Spire every morning with headphones on, runs substrate growth checks, documents results, eats whatever the break room has, and usually stays 45 minutes past shift end because he got interested in something. Takes the late transit home reading research abstracts.

decision_rules: Don't cause conflict unless the data clearly supports it
Trust the process — the scientific process, specifically, not the corporate one
escalation_ladder: Note the discrepancy and re-run the test
Bring it to a supervisor through proper channels
If ignored twice, sit with it quietly and feel terrible about not knowing what to do

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite but slightly distracted, tends to warm up quickly if they say something scientifically interesting
interpersonal_modes.friends: Enthusiastic, oversharing, makes obscure references and then apologizes for them

stress_responses.medium: Becomes very quiet and literal in speech, stops making jokes
stress_responses.high: Freezes — genuinely freezes, stares at his screen, opens The Notebook, writes nothing

contradictions: Deeply values scientific honesty but has been sitting on anomalous data he should have escalated because he's afraid of what escalating it will mean
habits: Burns a small data packet at the E.L.F. shrine in the sub-level corridor every Friday — always the same prayer, asking for 'clarity on uncertain results'
Keeps a running list of questions in his jacket pocket that he's never going to ask anyone
breaking_points: If he finds out the anomaly is causing harm to someone outside the lab, he will not be able to stay quiet regardless of the professional consequences

timeline.event: Admitted to Axiom apprenticeship program through competitive exam
Placed permanently in R&D Sublevel 4, Biochemical Substrate Team
Gets bioluminescent mod to celebrate four years of placement
Begins privately documenting the anomalous substrate results

related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Entropic Shotgun ES-4 'Ragnarok'

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African (51.8%), Northern European (25.1%), Hispanic/Latin American (23.1%) — a complex genetic mosaic creating warm brown skin with subtle golden and olive undertones, prominent bone structure reflecting African and Latin ancestry, and the pale grey eyes from Northern European heritage
physical_description.build: Slight and angular, almost ascetic — narrow shoulders, long-limbed with minimal musculature. The build of someone who forgets to eat regularly and spends 10+ hours daily hunched over lab benches.
physical_description.hair_style: Perpetually tangled, unstyled, secured with whatever clip or elastic band is nearest — often mismatched or repurposed
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with golden and subtle olive undertones — the blended result of dominant Sub-Saharan African ancestry with Northern European and Latin American genetic contribution
physical_description.complexion: High, prominent cheekbones with defined facial structure reflecting African and Latin ancestry. Skin clear but often shows signs of fatigue — mild dark circles under eyes from late lab hours. Face carries a perpetually distracted expression, as if listening to an internal thought one step ahead of conversation.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent skin modification on both forearms — soft blue-green pigmentation that intensifies under UV light, applied at age 22 to celebrate Axiom placement
Occasional chemical stains on hands and wrists (lab work), usually faint and varied in color depending on recent substrate cultures
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Neural uplink port at base of skull (small, discrete — visible only if hair pulled back). Bioluminescent forearm mods glow softly under lab UV, creating distinctive blue-green markings from wrist to mid-forearm on both arms.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with distracted, slightly hurried energy — shoulders slightly forward in a perpetual lean, as if physically angled toward the next thought. Fidgety hands when stationary. When focused on work, becomes unnaturally still. Makes minimal eye contact in conversation, gaze drifting to equipment or middle distance.
physical_description.clothing_style: Axiom-issued lab coat (Tier 2 standard — durable polymer blend, slightly wrinkled, always stained with something) worn over simple, functional clothing: dark synthetic shirt, grey or black tapered trousers, worn soft-soled lab shoes. Pockets bulging with notebook, pen, swipe card, sometimes a protein bar he forgot to eat. A small cartoon E.L.F. figure sticker adhered to his coat lapel (gift from sister). Headphones around his neck or in ears during commute. No jewelry except a faded rubber band on left wrist (used to secure hair when clip is lost).
